concerns.concern: The claim that switching becomes deterministic rests only on the cycle-to-cycle speckle correlation. No electrical switching statistics are shown, such as per-cycle On/Off resistance or the threshold/delay spread narrowing over the same cycle window.
concerns.quote: "Deterministic switching" is inferred only from speckle correlation; no switching statistics are shown.

concerns.concern: The rising cycle-to-cycle correlation could come from causes other than learning: incomplete relaxation between pulses, cumulative heating, irreversible electroforming, or X-ray dose. Because the Off state is never imaged, persistence cannot be told apart from reproducible re-formation.
concerns.quote: The Off state is never imaged, so persistence cannot be distinguished from reproducible re-formation.

concerns.concern: No train, erase with sub-threshold current, then re-cycle experiment is shown. The claims that sub-threshold current erases the memory and the device can be reset are therefore unsupported.
concerns.quote: Without this, "in-device learning" and "reset" remain speculation.

concerns.concern: The fitted relaxation times lie far beyond the measurement windows. In that regime β and τ are nearly degenerate and are fixed only by a tiny decay in g₂.
concerns.quote: β and τ are then almost perfectly degenerate and are set by a decay of a few ×10⁻³ in g₂.

concerns.concern: A single τ is imposed for all aging times while β is allowed to vary. Real aging of τ would then be absorbed into β, so the rise of β from 1 to 1.5 may be a fitting artefact.
concerns.quote: A drift of β from 1 to 1.5 could be a fitting artefact of this constraint.

concerns.concern: The correlation normalization uses a global average rather than the standard pixel-wise, ROI-based form. This makes it sensitive to total-intensity changes (phase fraction, Debye–Waller, beam decay), and the ROI is not specified.
concerns.quote: As written, G is sensitive to changes in total intensity

concerns.concern: The ~1000 s delay attributed to short-term memory could simply be slow thermal equilibration after a power step. Controls are needed that separate Joule heating from current-specific effects, such as a temperature step matched to the same device resistance.
concerns.quote: Without this, "memory" and "erasure" cannot be separated from thermal transients.

concerns.concern: Hours of focused X-ray exposure could itself drive the dynamics, since X-ray-induced persistent conductivity and structural changes in VO₂ are documented. A dose-dependence control is needed.
concerns.quote: A dose-dependence control is needed: attenuated flux, beam-off intervals, or a fresh spot.

concerns.concern: Thermal and positional drift from Joule heating or temperature changes shifts the Bragg peak and speckle on the detector, which can mimic decorrelation. Drift is not tracked or corrected.
concerns.quote: Both shift the Bragg peak and speckle on the detector and mimic decorrelation.

concerns.concern: Labelling the dynamics a jamming transition needs more than β. The Q-dependence of τ and a dynamic-heterogeneity analysis are needed.
concerns.quote: Calling this a jamming transition also needs more than β

concerns.concern: The beam footprint is larger than the 5×5 µm² gap and includes non-switching film. The filament is only a small fraction of the scattering volume, which may dilute or bias the correlation changes.
concerns.quote: It covers film under or outside the electrodes that never switches, and the filament occupies a small fraction of it.

concerns.concern: Ga irradiation, introduced to localize the filament, offers a conventional defect-pinning explanation for increasingly reproducible filament formation. The pristine-device data that would test this appear only in the SI and should be in the main text with the same analysis.
concerns.quote: Defect pinning is therefore an obvious, conventional explanation for increasingly reproducible filament formation.

concerns.concern: Only one training run on one device is shown. The number of devices and runs measured, and the spread in the cycle number at which learning occurs, are not reported.
concerns.quote: Only one training run on one device is shown.

concerns.concern: The definition and normalization of ΔG(n,n+1) are not given. If it is min–max scaled, a value near 1 does not mean deterministic, so the absolute correlation should be compared with the static-sample ceiling.
concerns.quote: If it is min–max scaled to [0,1], a value near 1 does not mean "deterministic."

concerns.concern: The treatment of the contrast A and the baseline in the fits (fixed or free) is not stated.
concerns.quote: The treatment of the contrast A and the baseline (fixed at 1 or free) is not stated.

concerns.concern: It is not established which Bragg peaks (M1 vs R) are in the analysed region. If only one is present, metallic and insulating rearrangement cannot be distinguished, and statements about metallic domains moving are speculative.
concerns.quote: If only one peak is in the ROI, the measurement cannot distinguish metallic from insulating rearrangement.

concerns.concern: The activation energy rests on essentially two temperatures. One point is the experimental stability limit, not a material relaxation time, and the other is non-stationary mid-transition, so more stationary temperatures are needed.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 2d inset appears to contain very few temperatures.

concerns.concern: Comparing the activation energy with the melting temperature, and inferring that melting occurs when domains become freely mobile, has no physical basis. It should be removed or justified.
concerns.quote: Activation barriers for domain-wall motion are not generally tied to the melting temperature.

concerns.concern: The order of runs on the irradiated device, and any resets between them, are not reported. This matters because the initial state of the cycling run may be history-dependent.
concerns.quote: the order of the runs on the irradiated device matters

concerns.concern: The jamming times for different currents are not statistically distinct, so a current dependence is not supported.
concerns.quote: The t_jam values (1100 ± 600, 1200 ± 500, 4000 ± 3000 s) are not statistically distinct.

concerns.concern: At 4 mA, β never reaches 1.5 within the measurement window, so the claim that all currents show the 1 to 1.5 transition is not shown.
concerns.quote: For 4 mA, β never reaches 1.5 within the 7000 s window

concerns.concern: The 0.26 mA run is sub-threshold with no filament. Including it contradicts the claim that electrical switching induces the jamming transition.
concerns.quote: Its inclusion contradicts "Electrical switching induces a jamming transition."

concerns.concern: 1.7 mA appears to be at or below the switching threshold. The authors should state whether it switches; if not, the β evolution is not switching-specific.
concerns.quote: If it does not, the β evolution is not switching-specific.

concerns.concern: The shear-thickening analogy is unsupported. It should be removed or backed by a defined driving rate and more currents.
concerns.quote: The shear-thickening analogy should be removed, or supported by a defined "driving rate" and more currents.

concerns.concern: The 1.7 mA two-time correlation data are not shown anywhere and should be included.
concerns.quote: The 1.7 mA two-time data are not shown anywhere and should be included.

concerns.concern: The cycling duty cycle and exposure timing are ambiguous: the On and Off durations, and when the 1 s exposure starts within the On phase, are unclear.
concerns.quote: The cycling duty cycle is ambiguous: "turned on and off for 3 s," with 1 s acquisition.

concerns.concern: The quoted domain size is a structural coherence length that includes strain broadening along an unspecified direction. It is not necessarily the metallic/insulating domain size.
concerns.quote: It is not necessarily the metallic/insulating domain size.

concerns.concern: Real-space imaging of the filament in trained and untrained states is suggested, so that speckle reproducibility can be tied to a reproducible filament location rather than inferred.
concerns.quote: Speckle reproducibility could then be tied to a reproducible filament location rather than inferred.

concerns.concern: The novelty claim that such dynamics are newly observed in hard matter ignores extensive prior XPCS work on compressed-exponential and aging dynamics in hard condensed matter.
concerns.quote: "Remarkably... here it is observed in hard matter" overlooks extensive prior XPCS reports

concerns.concern: The domain speeds mentioned in the text are never reported.
concerns.quote: The "domain speeds" mentioned in the Methods-referenced text are never reported

concerns.concern: Fitted τ values at 4 mA exceed the stated stability limit and should be described as lower bounds.
concerns.quote: τ values at 4 mA exceed the stated stability limit and should be described as lower bounds.

concerns.concern: Numerical values are inconsistent between text and figures: the stability-limit τ, the 4 mA τ, and the sub-threshold current (0.27 vs 0.26 mA).
concerns.quote: the sub-threshold current is 0.27 mA in the text but 0.26 mA in Figs. 3 and 4

concerns.concern: Text errors: a referenced inset does not exist, "stabilizes for" should read "after" ≈1000 cycles, and 200 cycles corresponds to ~600 s, not 1000 s.
concerns.quote: at ~3 s/cycle 200 cycles ≈ 600 s.

concerns.concern: The irradiation geometry is described inconsistently: a central 5×5 µm region in the main text versus global irradiation in Methods.
concerns.quote: while Methods says "devices were globally irradiated," even though one device is pristine.

concerns.concern: The aging-time construction is misdefined and needs a precise definition.
concerns.quote: Lines starting at t₁ = t₂ = t_age cannot satisfy t₁ + t₂ = t_age

concerns.concern: Eq. 3 is wrongly called a single exponential when it is a stretched/compressed exponential.
concerns.quote: it is a stretched/compressed (KWW) exponential.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1 panel labels do not match the caption.
concerns.quote: Fig. 1 panels are labelled c, d, e, but the caption describes them as top, center and bottom of panel c.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 5 caption does not match panel b, which plots voltage. The measurement temperature and ramp rate for Fig. 5b are missing.
concerns.quote: does not match panel b, which plots voltage.

concerns.concern: A table of all fit parameters per aging time and condition is requested, together with the temperatures used in the Arrhenius inset.
concerns.quote: Please supply a table of all fit parameters (A, τ, β, baseline) per t_age and condition

concerns.concern: The Bragg reflection indices relative to the substrate and the incidence angle should be specified, so the beam footprint can be evaluated.
concerns.quote: Specify the Bragg reflection indices relative to the R-cut substrate and the incidence angle
